title: LCM-NanoPOTS workflow for spatial proteome
author: Yumi Kwon
materials: Find the target region on scanned image
Navigate to the region of interest (ROI).
Start the collection with CenterRoboLPC function.

An Orbitrap Eclipse Tribrid mass spectrometer (Thermo scientific) with FAIMS-pro interface operated in data-dependent acquisition mode was used for all analyses. Peptides were ionized by applying a voltage of 2,400 V.

steps.title: Load DMSO Capture Media
steps.instruction: Place 100 µL of DMSO in the sample plate, dispense 200 nL of DMSO into each well of the nanoPOTS chip, then cover the chip with a sterile glass slide and aluminum foil.

steps.title: Prepare NanoPOTS Robot
steps.instruction: Set the nanoPOTS robot to the required temperature and humidity, and align the nanoPOTS chip on the robot deck.

steps.title: Configure Laser Capture Microdissection
steps.instruction: Turn on the PALM MicroBeam LCM, draw a 4 × 9 grid (voxel size = 2500 µm²) on the region of interest, and load the laser settings: Speed 1, Cut energy 40, LPC Energy delta 15.

steps.title: Collect Tissue Voxels
steps.instruction: Load the nanoPOTS chip onto slide collector 48, align the A1 corner of the collector with the A2 well corner of the chip, cut and collect all voxels, then inspect under a microscope that each DMSO droplet contains the tissue voxel.

steps.title: Post‑Collection Chip Handling
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the nanoPOTS chip from the collector, keep it covered with the glass slide, and place it in an incubator set to 70 °C.

steps.title: Initial DMSO Evaporation and Storage
steps.instruction: Wrap the chip with foil and store at –20 °C until analysis; later, after DMSO has evaporated, scan the chip to verify no wells are missing.

steps.title: Accelerated DMSO Removal
steps.instruction: Unwrap the chip after 15 min, place it uncovered in the 70 °C incubator for 5‑minute intervals until DMSO fully evaporates (≈19 min total), then place the chips upside‑down (still wrapped) in the incubator for an additional 15 min.

steps.title: Transfer Chip to NanoPOTS Robot
steps.instruction: Remove the chips from the incubator and load them into the nanoPOTS robot.

steps.title: Add Formic Acid
steps.instruction: Dispense 50 nL of 5 % formic acid in water into each well, then cover with a sterile glass slide, wrap with foil, and store at –20 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Heat Extraction Buffer Incubation
steps.instruction: Place the chip upside‑down in a humidity box inside a zip‑lock bag at 70 °C for 60 min, then cover with a glass slide and aluminum foil.

steps.title: Dispense Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Dispense 200 nL of extraction buffer (1 mM TCEP, 0.1 % DDM, 0.1 M HEPES, pH 8.5) into each well; also place 100 µL of the same extraction buffer in the sample plate.

steps.title: Room‑Temperature Dark Incubation
steps.instruction: Align the chip, set it at room temperature, load it into the nanoPOTS robot, then place it upside‑down in the dark for 30 min at room temperature; finally, cover with a glass slide and wrap with foil.

steps.title: Add Alkylation Buffer
steps.instruction: Dispense 50 nL of alkylation buffer (10 mM CAA in 0.1 M HEPES) into each well and add 100 µL of the same buffer to the sample plate.

steps.title: Alkylation Incubation
steps.instruction: Load the chip into the nanoPOTS robot, then place it upside‑down in a humidity box for 10 h at 37 °C; cover with a glass slide and foil during incubation.

steps.title: Add Digestion Buffer
steps.instruction: Dispense 50 nL of digestion buffer (0.01 ng/nL LysC, 0.04 ng/nL trypsin in 0.1 M HEPES) into each well and add 100 µL of the same buffer to the sample plate.

steps.title: Dry Digestion Droplets
steps.instruction: Remove the chip from the nanoPOTS robot and place it in a desiccator until all droplets have evaporated.

steps.title: LC‑MS Sample Loading
steps.instruction: Use the in‑house nanoPOTS autosampler equipped with a 100 µm × 4 cm, 5 µm, 300 Å C18 SPE column and a 50 µm × 25 cm, 1.7 µm, 190 Å C18 analytical column heated to 50 °C; dissolve samples on‑chip with Buffer A (0.1 % formic acid in water), trap on SPE for 5 min, wash, then elute at 100 nL/min with a 60‑min gradient from 8 % to 35 % Buffer B (0.1 % formic acid in acetonitrile).

steps.title: FAIMS‑Pro Ion Acquisition
steps.instruction: Acquire ions using the FAIMSpro interface with three compensation voltages (‑45, ‑60, ‑75 V); scan m/z 350‑1600 at 120 000 resolution, ion‑trap injection time 118 ms, AGC target 1 × 10⁶.

steps.title: Spectral Library Generation
steps.instruction: For pooled tissue samples, use a single CV per LC‑MS run; select precursor ions >1 × 10⁴ for 30 % HCD fragmentation, scan in the ion trap with AGC 2 × 10⁵ and injection time 86 ms.

steps.title: Process Data with FragPipe
steps.instruction: Run FragPipe v17.1 (MSFragger v3.4, Philosopher v4.1.0) for feature detection, database searching, and quantification; use the latest UniProt human database, fixed carbamidomethylation on cysteine, variable N‑terminal acetylation and methionine oxidation, strict trypsin (peptide length 7‑50, max 2 missed cleavages, FDR 0.01).

steps.title: Quantify with Match‑Between‑Runs
steps.instruction: Enable Match‑Between‑Runs and MaxLFQ in FragPipe with minimum 1 ion, minimum 3 scans, m/z tolerance 10 ppm, RT tolerance 0.4 min, and MBR FDR at ion level 0.05.
